payload.name: Preserve future planned events when updating memory
payload.description: Apply during construction UPDATE/MERGE when an existing event memory contains a future plan and a new message describes a different past or present event.
content: Before updating an event memory, compare the new event's timing and activity with the existing memory. If they refer to different events (e.g., one is a future plan, the other is a past occurrence), do NOT replace the whole memory content.
Preserve the prior planned event by appending the new event as separate clauses or creating a separate memory, using MERGE/enrichment if appropriate, so both facts remain retrievable.
Use UPDATE only when the new information revises the same event (same activity and time); otherwise keep the old plan intact and add the new event side by side.

solves: During construction, an UPDATE to an event memory can overwrite a previously stored future plan when a later message describes a different event. The cause is replacing whole memory content with the new event, losing the older plan. The rule: before updating, compare temporal focus and subject; if distinct events, preserve the prior plan by appending or merging rather than replacing. Applies to any construction step where a memory containing a future plan is later modified by a separate activity.
